name: Good practice: choose a strong password
answer:
A strong password is above all a long password: length matters more than complicated characters.

The simplest method: the passphrase

Put together four or five unrelated words, for example "giraffe-drum-storm-lemon". It is easy to remember and very hard to guess. Avoid famous quotes, song lyrics and anything to do with you (first names, dates of birth, the company name).

The rules to remember

  • at least 14 characters, or four words;
  • a different password for each service: if one website is hacked, your other accounts stay protected;
  • never reuse your work password on a personal website.

The password manager

Nobody can remember dozens of different passwords. A password manager remembers them for you, so you only have one main password to memorise. Ask the support team which one is approved in the company.

name: Good practice: never share your password
answer:
Your password is personal: it proves that it really is you doing something. Everything done with your account is attributed to you.

Nobody needs your password

  • IT support will never ask you for it, not by phone, not by email, not by message. Technicians have their own tools to work on your computer.
  • A colleague who needs a file or access should request it for themselves: do not lend them your session.
  • Nor does your manager: an absence is handled with a delegation or a shared folder, not by handing over a password.

If someone asks you for it

It is probably a scam attempt. Do not reply, and report it to the support team from the portal ("Report an issue").

If you gave it out by mistake

Change it immediately and let the support team know: reporting it is not a fault, it is the right thing to do.

name: Good practice: lock your session as soon as you leave your desk
answer:
A computer left unlocked, even for two minutes, lets anyone read your messages, send an email in your name or copy files.

The right habit, every time you get up

  • On Windows: press Windows + L.
  • On a Mac: press Ctrl + Cmd + Q.

Your work stays open: you just type your password again when you come back.

Also

  • Do not leave your laptop unattended on a train, in a café or in a meeting room.
  • Put sensitive paper documents away before you leave in the evening.
  • Automatic locking after a few minutes is a safeguard, not a nuisance: do not try to turn it off.

name: Good practice: why you are not an administrator of your computer
answer:
Your account does not have administrator rights on your computer. This is not a lack of trust: it is the principle of least privilege, one of the most effective protections.

What it is for

Malicious software acts with the rights of the person who opened it. Without administrator rights, it cannot install itself deeply, turn off the antivirus or spread easily. A simple wrong click therefore stays contained.

You need to install software or change a setting

  • Make the request from the portal, in the service catalog ("Request a service").
  • Say which software or setting, and why you need it.
  • The support team installs it for you, or gives you temporary rights if this is justified.

Never install software found on the Internet to get around this limit: that is exactly what attackers are looking for.

name: Good practice: multi-factor authentication
answer:
Multi-factor authentication adds a second proof to your password: a code sent to your phone, a notification to approve or a security key. Even if someone steals your password, they cannot sign in without this second element.

The right habits

  • Never approve a sign-in request that you did not start yourself, even if it keeps coming back: it is a sign that someone knows your password. Decline it, then report it to the support team.
  • Never give out a code received by text message or in the app, to anyone, even someone claiming to be from support.

You have lost or changed your phone

Let the support team know the same day, from the portal or by phone. They will deactivate the old device and help you register the new one. Do not wait until you are locked out to report it.

name: Good practice: recognise and report phishing
answer:
Phishing is a message that imitates a trusted sender to get you to click a link, open an attachment or give away a password. It is the number one way in for attacks.

Warning signs

  • a sense of urgency: "your account will be deleted today", "overdue payment";
  • a sender address that looks like the real one, but not quite;
  • a link whose real address (visible by hovering over the link without clicking) does not match the expected website;
  • an unusual request: changing bank details, buying gift cards, giving out a code;
  • an unexpected attachment, even from a known contact.

What to do

  • Do not click and do not open the attachment.
  • If in doubt, contact the sender another way (their usual number, not the one in the message).
  • Report the message to the support team from the portal ("Report an issue").

Have you already clicked or typed in your password? Let the support team know immediately: a few minutes can make all the difference.

name: Good practice: USB sticks and removable media
answer:
A USB stick can contain malicious software that runs as soon as it is plugged in. It is also easily lost, along with the data on it.

The rules to follow

  • Never plug in a stick that you found or received without asking for it: hand it to the support team.
  • Only use media supplied or approved by the company.
  • Do not copy company data onto a personal stick.
  • To exchange files, use the company's shared spaces rather than a USB stick.

If you lose a stick or a drive

Report it to the support team straight away, saying what was on it. If it held personal or confidential data, the company may have to report it within a short deadline.

name: Good practice: do not put off updates
answer:
Updates fix security flaws that attackers know about and sometimes exploit the very day after they are published. A computer that is not up to date is an open door.

What we ask of you

  • When your computer offers to restart to finish an update, do it as soon as possible, for example at break time or at the end of the day.
  • Do not put off an update several days in a row.
  • Also update your work phone and its apps.

If an update causes a problem

Has a piece of software stopped working, or is your computer very slow after restarting? Report it to the support team from the portal rather than trying to roll back yourself.

name: Good practice: remote working, public Wi-Fi and VPN
answer:
Outside the office, your connections go through networks that the company does not control. A few simple rules keep them protected.

The VPN

The VPN creates an encrypted tunnel between your computer and the company network. Always connect it before accessing the company's applications and files.

Public Wi-Fi networks

  • In a station, a hotel or a café, open Wi-Fi can be listened in on or imitated by a fake access point.
  • Use your work phone's hotspot instead.
  • If you do use public Wi-Fi, turn on the VPN before anything else.

At home and when travelling

  • Do not let family or friends use your work computer.
  • Watch out for prying eyes and ears on public transport and in public places: you can ask the support team for a privacy screen filter.

name: Good practice: where to save your documents
answer:
A document saved only on your computer disappears with it in the event of a breakdown, theft or ransomware. The company's storage spaces, on the other hand, are backed up.

Where to save

  • your work documents: in your personal company space or in your department's shared folders;
  • not on the desktop or in your computer's "Downloads" folder, which are usually not backed up;
  • never on a personal storage service (private online account, personal email).

You deleted or overwrote a file by mistake

If it was in a backed-up space, the support team can often restore it. Make the request quickly from the portal, giving the file name, its location and the date when it was still correct.

name: Good practice: personal data day to day (GDPR)
answer:
Personal data is any information that can identify a person: name, address, phone number, customer number, photo, health or payroll data. The GDPR requires it to be protected.

Day to day

  • Only access the data you need for your work.
  • Do not send customer or employee files to a personal address, or through an unapproved service.
  • Check the recipients before sending an email containing personal data.
  • Do not keep copies "just in case": delete what is no longer needed.
  • Print as little as possible and collect your printouts straight away.

If you make a mistake

An email sent to the wrong person, a file shared too widely, a lost computer: let the support team know immediately. A personal data breach sometimes has to be reported to the supervisory authority within 72 hours.

name: Good practice: what to do in the event of a security incident
answer:
A security incident is, for example: a computer that is unusually slow or shows unknown windows, files that can no longer be opened, a message demanding a ransom, an email sent in your name, or the loss or theft of a computer or phone.

The right reflexes

  • Let the support team know immediately, from the portal ("Report an issue") or by phone if you can no longer use your computer.
  • Ransom message or files that cannot be opened: unplug the network cable and turn off Wi-Fi, but do not switch off the computer unless the support team tells you to.
  • Never pay a ransom and do not reply to the attackers.
  • Do not try to fix it yourself and do not delete anything: the traces help to understand what happened.
  • Note the time and what you saw; a photo of the screen taken with your phone can help.

No shame in reporting

Anyone can be caught out. What matters is speed: an incident reported within minutes causes far less damage than one discovered days later.
